subject: Career
title: The Proximity Principle
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Proximity Principle.

hook.text: MIT researchers found: people one floor apart collaborate 50% less than those on the same floor.

buildup.text: The proximity principle: physical closeness dramatically predicts relationship formation.

discovery.text: Tom Allen's research at MIT showed communication drops exponentially with distance — even meters matter.

twist.text: Remote work breaks proximity. Without deliberate effort, remote workers become network-invisible.

climax.text: Virtual proximity requires intention: regular calls, shared channels, and visible contributions.

punchline.text: Proximity builds bonds. Distance requires intention.

quiz.question: What did Tom Allen's research show about workplace proximity?
options: Communication drops exponentially with physical distance

details.summary: The proximity principle states that you are most likely to form relationships with people physically or digitally close to you. Shared spaces like offices, co-working areas, and online communities create repeated casual interactions that build trust over time.
details.whyItMatters: Proximity explains why remote workers and freelancers must be more intentional about networking. Without the natural collisions of a shared space, relationships require deliberate effort.
takeaways: Physical proximity increases relationship formation probability dramatically
Remote professionals must engineer digital proximity through communities
Co-working spaces and industry meetups recreate casual proximity

faq.question: How do remote workers replicate the proximity effect for networking?
faq.answer: Join active Slack or Discord communities in your field, attend regular virtual coffee chats, and participate in co-working sessions. The goal is repeated casual interaction that mimics hallway conversations. Channels where the same people show up weekly work best.

faq.question: Does the proximity principle explain why some office seats lead to faster promotions?
faq.answer: Research supports this. People seated near decision-makers have more spontaneous interactions, leading to greater visibility and stronger relationships. This is why strategic seating choices and finding reasons to be near leadership can accelerate career growth.
